messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed direct C-H arylation of an imidazole to form 5-(2-fluorophenyl)-1-methyl-1H-imidazole-4-carbonitrile (Shields et al., Nature 2021, reaction 3); choose the base, ligand, solvent, concentration and temperature.

Variables and options:
base:
B1: cesium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[Cs+]]
B2: potassium pivalate [SMILES O=C([O-])C(C)(C)C.[K+]]
B3: cesium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[Cs+]]
B4: potassium acetate [SMILES O=C([O-])C.[K+]]

ligand:

L5: tBPh-CPhos [SMILES CN(C)C1=CC=CC(N(C)C)=C1C2=CC=CC=C2P(C(C)(C)C)C3=CC=CC=C3]

L8: CgMe-PPh [SMILES C[C@]1(O2)O[C@](C[C@]2(C)P3C4=CC=CC=C4)(C)O[C@]3(C)C1]
L9: JackiePhos [SMILES FC(F)(F)C1=CC(P(C2=C(C3=C(C(C)C)C=C(C(C)C)C=C3C(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC)C4=CC(C(F)(F)F)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C4)=CC(C(F)(F)F)=C1]
L10: PPh3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CC=C1)(C2=CC=CC=C2)C3=CC=CC=C3]
L11: P(fur)3 [SMILES P(C1=CC=CO1)(C2=CC=CO2)C3=CC=CO3]
L12: PCy3 HBF4 [SMILES P(C1CCCCC1)(C2CCCCC2)C3CCCCC3]

solvent:
S1: N,N-dimethylacetamide [SMILES CC(N(C)C)=O]
S2: p-xylene [SMILES CC1=CC=C(C)C=C1]
S3: butyronitrile [SMILES CCCC#N]

concentration:

picks.reason: This tests whether a compact, electron-rich dialkylphosphine can rival L4 under the best observed base, solvent, dilution, and temperature.
BrettPhos is a strongly donating bulky biaryl phosphine and is a promising alternative to L4 under the established best conditions.
X-Phos provides a distinct bulky biaryl-phosphine environment to screen while retaining the strongest observed reaction setup.
The electron-rich, sterically demanding tBPh-CPhos may support C–H arylation and is worth testing at the optimized conditions.
This tests whether a small dialkylaryl phosphine performs better than the previously tested bulky biaryl ligand under favorable conditions.
Testing PPh2Me at the optimized conditions separates ligand performance from the unfavorable conditions of its prior experiment.
The unusual chiral phosphine offers a distinct ligand structure to evaluate while holding all other conditions at their best observed values.
JackiePhos performed poorly in other settings, so this checks whether the optimal solvent, base, dilution, and temperature improve its outcome.
PPh3 is a conventional reference ligand and its performance under the strongest observed conditions will help assess the need for specialized ligands.
This screens a comparatively electron-rich tri(furyl)phosphine under the optimized reaction conditions.
PCy3 is a strongly donating, bulky phosphine and may provide a useful alternative to the successful L4 ligand.
DMAc may improve the solubility of ionic reagents relative to the best-performing ester solvent while retaining L4 and the optimized base.
This tests whether a less polar aromatic medium can improve the reaction with the otherwise best-performing catalyst system.
Butyronitrile provides a distinct coordinating solvent environment to compare with the successful butyl acetate.
Cesium acetate gave a strong yield at C1, and this tests whether its performance is retained at the next concentration.
This completes the concentration comparison for cesium acetate and checks whether the dilution benefit also applies to this base.
Potassium pivalate is the best base, but this tests whether cesium pivalate's weaker prior result was affected by concentration.
Potassium acetate gave no yield at C1, and a second concentration checks whether that failure is robust.
If BrettPhos is promising at C1, this adjacent concentration tests whether its performance follows the observed dilution trend.
This compares X-Phos at a second concentration to check whether its outcome depends on the strongly favorable dilution.
